parameters.name: Ts
parameters.description: Sampling period supplied in TASK.md; fixed because the timestamps are equally spaced.

parameters.name: gv
parameters.description: Forward-command scale, estimated jointly in this candidate; not imported from another fit.

parameters.name: gw
parameters.description: Angular-command scale, estimated jointly in this candidate; not imported from another fit.

parameters.name: ell
parameters.description: Effective half wheel separation in command-to-wheel-speed conversion, jointly estimated; not claimed to be the measured chassis geometry.

parameters.name: dz
parameters.description: Symmetric static dead-zone threshold, estimated jointly with the other fitted parameters.

parameters.name: bw
parameters.description: Constant angular-response offset, estimated jointly with all other fitted coefficients.

parameters.name: eps
parameters.description: Fixed numerical small-turn cutoff for the continuous zero-rate limit, chosen to avoid zero division; below this cutoff the sinc-factor error is less than 5e-16, dimensionless, by its Taylor expansion. This is not fitted.

estimation.criterion: Minimize the sum, over every step of every complete 25-transition window, of squared `x` error plus squared heading error multiplied by `(0.15)**2`. Here the fixed heading weight is 0.15 m/rad; `y` has zero weight. This emphasizes the scored `x` output but regularizes angular calibration using measured heading. The weight was selected from the three explicitly tested choices (equal `x`/`y` weights with 0.3 m/rad heading weight, `x` only, and `x` with 0.15 m/rad heading weight), judged using held-out whole trajectories and parsimony.
estimation.data: `data/train.csv`, all three trajectories and all 450 logged samples. Each trajectory is separate. Construct every complete overlapping window of 25 transitions (5 s), starting at sample indices 0 through 124: 125 windows per trajectory, 375 windows total. No window crosses a trajectory boundary. Each window starts from its logged pose; subsequent predictions use only simulated states. Unwrap `phi` within each trajectory before fitting; trigonometric position predictions are invariant to full turns. No rows are excluded. These windows target the intended simulation duration without treating noisy measured differences as exact velocities.
estimation.method: Bound-constrained nonlinear least squares with `scipy.optimize.least_squares`, trust-region reflective algorithm (`method = trf`), finite-difference Jacobian, linear squared-error loss, `max_nfev = 400`, and `ftol = xtol = gtol = 1e-10` (dimensionless stopping tolerances). All fitted parameters were estimated together in one step in this final candidate; there is no parameter transfer. Starting values: `gv = 0.9`, `gw = 0.8`, `ell = 0.12` m, `dz = 0.012` m/s, `bw = 0` rad/s. They come from diagnostic settled-command gains and small plausible offsets/thresholds, not held-out data. Bounds: `0.2 <= gv <= 1.5`, `0.2 <= gw <= 1.5`, `0.04 <= ell <= 0.3` m, `0 <= dz <= 0.06` m/s, `-0.15 <= bw <= 0.15` rad/s. Bounds enforce positive gains, moderate offsets and nondegenerate geometry while allowing timing adjustment; they are chosen constraints, not inferred confidence intervals. Nonlinear least squares is used because repeated state simulation and dead-zone/trigonometric terms depend nonlinearly on the coefficients; ordinary linear regression cannot optimize this rollout criterion. The procedure is deterministic and uses no random seed. `gv` and `gw` are dimensionless; `bw` is in rad/s; angular `dz` is in rad/s; wheel-model `dz` is in m/s; `ell` is in m; `q` is dimensionless, when present. For estimator comparison, refit from the same numerical starting values on each pair of trajectories and predict the third; the final reported coefficients use all three trajectories.

discussion.family: Differential-drive inverse kinematics, symmetric wheel-speed dead zones, and constant-twist arc integration. Unicycle/differential-drive kinematic model; see Steven M. LaValle, Planning Algorithms (2006), cited from memory without checking the book.
discussion.interpretation: The virtual right and left wheel speeds are `v_f+ell*v_a` and `v_f-ell*v_a`, where `ell` is effective half wheel separation. Each uses `sign(v_f+ell*v_a)*Max(Abs(v_f+ell*v_a)-dz,0)` or `sign(v_f-ell*v_a)*Max(Abs(v_f-ell*v_a)-dz,0)`. Their average times `gv` drives translation; their difference times `gw/(2*ell)` plus `bw` drives rotation. Constant-twist midpoint direction and sinc chord scaling then integrate the resulting twist. `dz` is an effective virtual-wheel speed threshold, not the angular threshold of the other nonlinear candidate. `ell`, `dz` and gains may trade off, since actual wheel-speed observations are absent.
discussion.origin: The translation-invariant terms `x` and `y`, the projection operators `cos` and `sin`, and heading accumulation came from planar differential-drive kinematics, not symbolic search. Initial diagnostics used within-trajectory pose differences and command-block phase. I compared Euler, constant-twist arc, affine bias, free phase, odd cubic, smooth dead-zone, angular/forward coupling, heading harmonics and lateral-slip structures. Sparse angular regression was diagnostic only; no genetic symbolic-regression search was used. Residuals were much larger at command changes and correlated within blocks, so final parameters were fitted to multi-step trajectories rather than one-step derivatives. A forward/angular coupling diagnostic suggested that independent angular dead zones might miss wheel-level interactions. The derived virtual wheel commands `v_f+ell*v_a` and `v_f-ell*v_a` motivated applying the same threshold to each wheel. This is a physical-structure hypothesis, not a direct measurement of either wheel or a searched algebraic expression. All three trajectories excite these virtual commands; retain the model as a modest nonlinear alternative, not as a proven motor friction law.
discussion.limitations: Training commands satisfy approximately `0.000034312 <= v_f <= 0.298155603` m/s and `-0.948147536 <= v_a <= 0.941160627` rad/s, computed on all training rows. Reverse motion and larger commands are not validated. Pose noise, actuator calibration drift and slip cannot be separated with these data. The expressions contain no previous command or actuator state: they cannot reproduce observed command carryover. Calibration coefficients are effective open-loop predictors, not uniquely identified mechanical parameters. Long-duration accuracy is not established by the 5 s fitting criterion. `phi_next` is deliberately unwrapped; periodic sine and cosine make position updates valid across heading wraps.
